overall_assessment: The Searchright benchmark evaluation harness implements strict anti-leakage invariants, deterministic sealed-split digest commitments, and schema-validated public report generation. The sealed manifest structure correctly segregates test labels from repository source trees, and metric calculations across binary classification, recall@k, and review burden behave analytically with zero non-finite outputs. Minor observations identify opportunities for streaming large evaluation batches and expanding synthetic multi-dialect test splits.

findings.description: Sealed label digest verification requires full in-memory collection of label vectors prior to hashing, which is optimal for bounded benchmarks (<100k items) but should offer chunked verification for multi-million record corpora.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a streaming hasher variant for large out-of-core evaluation sets in later tracks.

findings.description: The public benchmark report validation contract rejects empty metric sets but does not require an explicit environment or hardware digest field.
findings.recommendation: Add optional system_environment metadata schema validation for reproducible benchmarking.

findings.description: Anti-leakage code scanning in check_benchmark_governance.py correctly flags forbidden substring patterns in test fixtures.
findings.recommendation: Retain strict regex and string pattern exclusions across all future benchmark releases.

calibration_notes: Benchmark evaluators will endorse the mathematical rigor of the sealed digest and contamination checks. They will confirm that no external performance claims are made from synthetic fixtures alone.
